summary.title: Writing a Linux Debugger: Part 7 - Source-Level Breakpoints
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set breakpoints on function names and source lines by mapping them to addresses via DWARF debug info, and how to look up ELF symbols.
keywords: how to set breakpoint on source line in debugger
how to set breakpoint on function name
takeaways: Function breakpoints use DW_AT_low_pc, then skip the prologue by advancing one line table entry.
Source line breakpoints find the line table entry matching file and line with is_stmt set, then set a breakpoint at its address.
ELF symbols can be read from .symtab/.dynsym sections and mapped to a symbol type, name and address.
The debugger's break command infers breakpoint kind from its argument: hex address, file:line, or function name.
summary.summary: This post, part 7 of a series on building a Linux debugger in C++, adds source-level breakpoints. It uses the DWARF debug info (function address ranges and the line table) to translate function names and file:line pairs into machine addresses. It also adds a symbol lookup command that searches ELF symbol tables, using libelfin for parsing. The post ends with the command-parsing code and testing suggestions.
